memories.content: Keep the total, major cost categories, and one-line estimate basis in the main text so the resource argument can be understood without leaving the proposal.
Place each major cost beside the activity or deliverable it enables in the main text.
State the quantity and unit-rate basis for each major cost in the same paragraph that requests it.
Readers may question a proposed priority when its cost cannot be checked on the same page as the claimed benefit.
Update the cost sentence whenever the related activity changes so the narrative and requested amount cannot drift apart.
Accept a denser main-text paragraph when the estimate basis is essential to deciding whether the request is proportionate.
The user tends to revise the work plan but forget a detached budget table unless the key amount is repeated beside the activity.
Specify in one sentence the user population and actual usage environment to which the design knowledge applies.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through the specified target population and environment.
Specify the workflow, technical infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions that must match before applying the design guidelines at another field site.
The transferability of field design knowledge depends not only on user characteristics but also on workflow and technological–organizational infrastructure.
The user tends to apply results confirmed at one deployment site to all similar organizations.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational concerns: the reference frame governs how proposal costs remain visible, checkable, and synchronized with activities, while the compared frame defines and safeguards the transfer boundary for field-design knowledge. Neither frame contains a claim materially addressing the other’s decisions.

relations.reason: These claims jointly establish that decision-essential totals, major categories, and concise estimation logic belong in the proposal narrative rather than being sacrificed for brevity.
relations.summary: The main text should retain an understandable overview of the requested resources, even when the necessary estimate basis makes it denser.

relations.reason: The placement rule and reviewer-risk observation express one underlying requirement for locally checkable cost-to-benefit linkage.
relations.summary: Major costs should appear beside the activities or deliverables they enable so readers can assess costs against claimed benefits on the same page.

relations.reason: This is a specific one-sided requirement for granular estimate verification that is not addressed by the compared frame.
relations.summary: Each major cost request should state its quantity and unit-rate basis in the same paragraph.

relations.reason: The maintenance rule and observed tendency to overlook detached budget material describe the same drift-prevention concern.
relations.summary: Cost wording and key amounts should remain attached to revised activities so plan changes do not leave the budget narrative stale.

relations.reason: The specification requirement and reviewer rationale jointly concern how population and environment define the generalization boundary.
relations.summary: Design knowledge should state the user population and actual usage environment that bound its applicability.

relations.reason: These claims jointly define transferability through operational and technological-organizational conditions beyond user characteristics.
relations.summary: Applying design guidelines at another field site requires matching relevant workflow, technical infrastructure, and organizational authority conditions.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided behavioral observation about overgeneralization that neither duplicates the transfer criteria nor appears in the reference frame.
relations.summary: The user tends to generalize results from one deployment site across similar organizations.

reports.compared_only: Design knowledge should identify its population and environment, specify site-transfer conditions across workflow and infrastructure, and guard against unjustified generalization.
reports.reference_only: Proposal costs should remain explicit beside their activities and benefits, include a checkable estimate basis, and be updated with work-plan changes despite added textual density.
